paper.title: Growing Artificial Societies: Social Science from the Bottom Up

headline: Sugarscape (agent-based): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; Gini rises 0.23 -> 0.48 from a near-uniform start (inequality emerges); P3 top-decile share 0.27 < 0.3 MISS without agent replacement

verdicts.gate: P1 final mean Gini of wealth >= 0.40 (strong inequality emerges)
P2 final Gini - initial Gini >= 0.15 (inequality rises from uniform start)
P3 right-skewed wealth: mean > median AND top-decile share >= 0.30
reasons: mean wealth 169.98 vs median 162.25 (mean>median in 9/10 seeds); top-decile share = 0.2696 (>= 0.3 in 1/10 seeds); locked clause needs BOTH

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the emergent-inequality result and would catch an artifact. Basic rule M only (no agent replacement rule R), which is why the top-decile concentration is moderate.

citations: Epstein, J.M. & Axtell, R. (1996). Growing Artificial Societies: Social Science from the Bottom Up. Brookings Institution Press / MIT Press. ISBN 9780262550253. (Sugarscape: emergent wealth inequality, Chapter II.)

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction
